algorithm_long: DFT-Stack: a cross-fitted, simplex-weighted stack of composition experts for the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks, using Materials Project DFT data as transfer-learning input features. EXTERNAL DATA DISCLOSURE: besides the formula-derived descriptors, every expert receives a block of Materials Project PBE DFT features taken from matminer's matbench_mp_gap (PBE band gap) and matbench_mp_e_form (PBE formation energy) datasets, matched to each task composition by reduced formula (most stable polymorph by formation energy, plus polymorph aggregates; unmatched compositions get missing values and a dft_matched = 0 indicator). These DFT values are STRUCTURE-DERIVED: every Materials Project entry is a DFT calculation on a crystal structure, and per reduced formula we take the entry (polymorph) with the lowest formation energy per atom plus aggregates over all polymorphs of that formula (min/median/max gap, metallic fraction, number of polymorphs). The entry is therefore 'DFT, structure-derived, matched by formula', and the DFT gap / metal flag are close proxies of the matbench_expt_gap and matbench_expt_is_metal targets. No experimental external labels are used: the only experimental labels seen are the task's own training-fold labels. Features: matminer/pymatgen composition descriptors (Magpie and other ElementProperty presets, element fractions, Stoichiometry, ValenceOrbital, IonProperty, BandCenter, AtomicOrbitals, Meredig, Miedema, YangSolidSolution, AtomicPackingEfficiency, WenAlloys, TMetalFraction) and CBFV Oliynyk statistics; all are label-free functions of the formula. Experts: Optuna-tuned LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, extra trees (two feature sets and element fractions), kernel ridge (regression) or RBF SVM (classification), k-nearest neighbours and an MLP; for matbench_expt_gap additionally hurdle experts for the zero-inflated band gap (a classifier for gap > 0 combined with a regressor fitted on the non-zero gaps). Protocol: nested cross-validation inside each official training fold. Five inner folds produce out-of-fold predictions for every expert; hyperparameters, the non-negative stack weights (summing to one; L1 loss for regression, Brier score for classification) and an optional novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction are all chosen on these inner folds, and the correction is kept only if a further nested inner-CV check confirms it (it was kept in 0 of 20 task-folds). FOLD USE, STATED EXACTLY. Fold-internal (fitted on the training rows T_k of each official fold k only, test rows only predicted): the Optuna hyperparameters, the simplex stack weights, the correction gate and the classification thresholds. NOT fold-internal for folds 1-4: the coarse design choices that are fixed in the shipped configuration (the feature-block set BLOCKS2; for matbench_expt_gap the hurdle experts and the removal of the element-fraction extra-trees expert; the Optuna budget of 20 trials; dropping the random-forest expert; restricting CatBoost to the F1 feature set; the fixed SVC C and gamma) were made in a design phase on fold 0's training rows (inner pseudo-folds, no fold-0 test rows). Fold 0's training rows contain the test rows of folds 1-4, so for folds 1-4 these fixed choices were informed by rows that are later test rows; fold 0 is the only fold whose every choice was made without its test rows. Fold-0 vs 5-fold mean of the recorded entry: matbench_steels 93.36 vs 80.10 MAE; matbench_expt_gap 0.2099 vs 0.2352 MAE; matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9573 vs 0.9547 balanced accuracy; matbench_glass 0.9136 vs 0.8937 balanced accuracy. Classification: hard labels are recorded at a decision threshold that maximises balanced accuracy on the training-fold out-of-fold predictions (inner-CV threshold), so the board's ROC-AUC for these tasks equals balanced accuracy. The configuration was frozen (SHA-256 hashes of the code) before the official test folds were predicted with it, and the test folds were predicted once with this configuration.
notes: CPU-only (no GPU): 5 parallel workers x 4 threads on one Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-14650HX workstation (16 cores / 24 threads); 14.3 worker-hours for all 20 task-folds; median wall time per fold: matbench_steels 9 min, matbench_expt_gap 62 min, matbench_expt_is_metal 48 min, matbench_glass 57 min. Per-fold compute is recorded in the parameters of every fold in results.json.gz (wall_time_s, n_workers, threads_per_worker, cpu_threads_used, cpu_model, gpu, expert_fit_seconds per expert). DFT-block coverage (compositions matched by reduced formula): matbench_steels: 0/312 (0%); matbench_expt_gap: 3347/4604 (73%); matbench_expt_is_metal: 3613/4921 (73%); matbench_glass: 60/5680 (1%). PRIOR RUN ON THE OFFICIAL FOLDS: an earlier pre-registered configuration (Amendment 1: no DFT block, no hurdle experts, smaller expert pool, fully fold-internal candidate selection) was scored on the official test folds on 2026-10-18, before this configuration (Amendment 2) was designed and pre-registered. Its results, which are reported in the manuscript and in the research repository (results/final/): matbench_steels 82.80 MAE; matbench_expt_gap 0.3240 MAE; matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9370 balanced accuracy; matbench_glass 0.8841 balanced accuracy; probability ROC-AUC matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9825, matbench_glass 0.9567. The present configuration was then scored once; there was no further iteration on test scores. LABELS VARIANT: results.json.gz records hard labels for the two classification tasks (the 'labels' variant). A 'probabilities' variant (same predictions, probabilities recorded) was written at the same scoring moment and is kept in the research repository; recording labels was fixed in the pre-registered Amendment-2 protocol before scoring, because the board compares label-based entries by balanced accuracy. For reference, the probability ROC-AUC of the same predictions is matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9895 ± 0.0008, matbench_glass 0.9606 ± 0.0080, and matbench itself would score the probabilities file (thresholded at 0.5) at matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9559, matbench_glass 0.8725. TRANSDUCTIVE BUT LABEL-FREE IMPUTATION: two feature builders fill rare missing descriptor values with column medians computed over all rows of a task (training and test rows together; no labels): CBFV generate_features for the Oliynyk block and the 'extra' matminer block in dftstack/data.py. Cells filled, per task: matbench_steels: CBFV 0 of 96096 cells (0 rows), extra block 0 of 6552 cells (0 rows); matbench_expt_gap: CBFV 2782 of 1418032 cells (422 rows), extra block 42 of 96684 cells (14 rows); matbench_expt_is_metal: CBFV 3075 of 1515668 cells (465 rows), extra block 42 of 103341 cells (14 rows); matbench_glass: CBFV 132 of 1749440 cells (22 rows), extra block 63 of 119280 cells (21 rows). Columns that are entirely missing are dropped on the same basis. matbench==0.6 was installed with --no-deps because its scikit-learn==1.0 / monty pins do not build on Python 3.12; the newer versions listed in requirements were used. The folder is self-contained: run_submission.py plus the dftstack/ package (verbatim copies of the frozen research modules) reproduce results.json.gz and record every fold with task.record; the Matbench tasks and the matminer DFT datasets are downloaded on first use. Full research repository (analysis plan, freeze hashes, per-fold predictions, ablations): https://github.com/bhaskargurram-ai/matbench-composition-stack. The matbench 0.6 wheel writes plain JSON even for a .gz filename; the file here is the byte-identical JSON gzip-compressed, which is what MatbenchBenchmark.from_file on the current main branch reads (run_submission.py compresses its output the same way).
